clauses.statement: When the server cannot resume an offered session and the client supplies a usable full-handshake offer, the server may proceed with a full handshake under a different session ID. A server may also return an empty ID for an uncached new session. Preserve the actual ClientHello in the Finished transcript.

evidence.scope: Legacy full-handshake fallback for WinWAP offers with short or eight-byte stale IDs, tested with captured ClientHello-derived fixtures. Live XP verification of a stale-ID offer and an abbreviated wire handshake are separate milestones.

clauses.statement: A critical connection_close_notify ends the current connection. Session closure also invalidates the session ID. On a later ClientHello the server selects a distinct ID for a new full handshake when it cannot resume the offered session.

evidence.scope: The opt-in probe sends a protected connection close and starts a fresh peer. The buffered XP run completed full handshakes and protected WSP replies before and after the close.
evidence.peerObservation: WinWAP 4.2.0.290 sent empty IDs on every captured ClientHello. WTLS-201 stale-ID fallback remains covered by Rust fixtures. Two direct trials showed a separate clear-alert retry failure. The buffered trial completed both protected exchanges.

clauses.statement: A ClientHello announces the ordered key exchanges and an optional existing session ID. A matching ServerHello ID and abbreviated Finished flight provide observable evidence of session reuse. Authenticated suite offers and a completed certificate-authenticated exchange are distinct evidence.

evidence.scope: Ruflo reviewed the candidate screen. The maintainer ran RIM's stock BlackBerry 7290 simulator in isolated XP and decoded its captured full-handshake offers. The authenticated lab endpoint reported UnsupportedProfile before any ServerHello.
evidence.peerObservation: BlackBerry offered authenticated RSA and 3DES-CBC-EDE with full SHA. The three distinct ClientHellos all had empty IDs. Certificate verification, protected application traffic, and live resumption remain open.

clauses.statement: A full-handshake ServerHello identifies a selected offered key by its one-based index, chooses offered algorithms, and uses a key-refresh value no greater than the client's. The Finished calculation covers the actual handshake messages. A full exchange on cache miss selects a different session ID.

evidence.scope: Authenticated suite selection and exact transcript with live BlackBerry full handshakes, protected WSP traffic and cache-miss fallback. Ruflo verified the exact candidate and 57 locked offline Cargo tests passed.
evidence.peerObservation: Operator compared the displayed leaf thumbprint and accepted the lab certificate at the stock trust prompt for each full handshake. BlackBerry reoffered ac51a992d73be1a9 after protected connection closure. The server sent 7877de87c4ade752 and completed a second full handshake. Automatic CA trust and wire resumption remain open.

clauses.statement: A matched session ID allows a server-first abbreviated Finished exchange under the cached master secret. Fresh hello randoms produce connection-local keys and current record epochs. Protected connection close preserves a cacheable session while protected session close invalidates it.

evidence.scope: Authenticated cache and abbreviated wire exchange, verified with deterministic native peers. WTLS-206 tracks the BlackBerry key-index observation.

clauses.statement: An abbreviated ServerHello may use zero for the ignored key field. If there is a matching offered key exchange, the server can return its one-based index. The echoed session ID and server-first Finished flight still identify resumption.

evidence.scope: Native tests verify the resumed index with full and abbreviated-only offers. The reviewed code also resumed a real cached BlackBerry connection after a protected connection close.
evidence.peerObservation: Both reconnect hellos carried a3ae109830b84aa6. The server committed first, verified the client Finished and received the acknowledgement for its protected WSP reply.
